chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil and Hisham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding what people narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'People of two religions do not inherit from each other.' He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'We inherit them and they do not inherit us, for Islam has only increased him in honor in his right.'

Second: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Jews and Christians do not inherit the Muslims, and the Muslim inherits the Jew and the Christian.'

Third: Yunus from Zura'a from Sama'a who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Muslim man, does he inherit the polytheist? He said: 'Yes, and the polytheist does not inherit the Muslim.'

Fourth: From him, from Musa ibn Bakr from Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yan who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, if a Christian dies and he has a Muslim son, does he inherit him?' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah the Exalted has not increased him by Islam except in honor, so we inherit them and they do not inherit us.'

Fifth: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Wallad who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muslim inherits his dhimmi (non-Muslim subject) wife, and she does not inherit him.'

Sixth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim blocks (excludes) the disbeliever and inherits him, and the disbeliever does not block the believer and does not inherit him.'

Seventh: As for what al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: I asked him, 'Do people of two religions inherit from each other?' He said: 'No.'

Eighth: From him, he said: Abdallah ibn Jabala narrated to them from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Muslim husband and the Jewish or Christian wife, that he said: 'They do not inherit from each other.'

key_terms.مِيرَاثُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: inheritance of Abu Talib (used as an example)

ai.seo_question: Do Muslims inherit non-Muslims and vice versa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This compilation from al-Istibsar elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'asabiyya' (solidarity) in inheritance, establishing that a Muslim inherits a non-Muslim (Ahl al-Kitab or polytheist), but the reverse is not true, based on the Prophetic maxim that Islam increases one in honor. The text reconciles apparent contradictions by distinguishing between mutual inheritance (tawarith) and unilateral inheritance, while also addressing specific juristic nuances such as the exclusion of spouses in certain contexts and the application of tawqiyya (dissimulation) to align with Sunni views where appropriate.
